newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London had another quiet day with no fresh fundamental news affecting prices. December lost 90 cents to close at $316.00. The fact that Brazil approved a final tranche of 1.04 million tonnes of tax-free sugar exports from the 5.2 million export limit had no discernable impact on prices. The market also ignored news of damage to the Cuban sugar cane crop following a hurricane after Havana said the island still aimed to improve on last year's 4.5 million tonnes. The New York raw sugar market was dull and range- bound. March closed up 2 points at 10.65 cents/lb, while May ended 5 points higher at 10.70 cents/lb. The deferreds closed 1 to 4 points higher. Support remained at 10.50 cents/lb in March and resistance at 10.80 cents/lb. without fresh constructive news in the market could well drift lower.

DENMARK - Sugar exports in July 1996 reached 13,860 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 15,016 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in October/July 1995/96 up to 135,403 tonnes against 170,138 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 199,559 tonnes compared to 255,177 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/July 1995/96 were Norway with 94,823 tonnes whites against 92,213 tonnes and Ireland with 7,536 tonnes, up from 7,260 tonnes.

NETHERLANDS - Sugar imports in June 1996 amounted to 3,120 tonnes which brought cumulative imports in the first three quarters of 1995/96 (October/June) up to 46,239 tonnes, hardly changed from last year's 44,280 tonnes. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 64,568 tonnes against 79,854 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October/June 1995/96 were France with 17,844 tonnes whites against 16,262 tonnes and Belgium/Luxembourg with 14,505 tonnes compared to 12,446 tonnes. Sugar exports in June 1996 reached 7,323 tonnes, sharply down from last year's 64,443 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in October June 1995/96 up to 274,203 tonnes against 347,439 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 381,586 tonnes against 654,277 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/June 1995/96 were Iran with 61,805 tonnes whites against 90,802 tonnes, Libya with 25,239 tonnes, up from 12 tonnes and Turkey with 23,518 tonnes compared to 20,015 tonnes.

FINLAND - Sugar exports in October/June 1995/96 amounted to 37,222 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 5,623 tonnes. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 6,763 tonnes against 15,127 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in the first three quarters of 1995/96 (October/June) were Uzbekistan with 11,381 tonnes whites against nil, Russia with 8,495 tonnes compared to 551 tonnes and Estonia with 8,194 tonnes against 754 tonnes. Sugar imports in October/June 1995/96 amounted to 16,999 tonnes, sharply down from last year's 51,608 tonnes. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 52,647 tonnes against 116,817 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October/June 1995/96 were Guyana with 10,326 tonnes raws against nil and St. Christopher Nevis with 5,311 tonnes compared to nil.

CUBA - The Cuban Sugar Ministry is reported to have stated that it will have to revise its estimate of sugar production in 1996/97, as a consequence of the damage sustained as a result of widespread flooding and wind damage. Hurricane Lili struck the provinces of Havana, Villa Clara, Matanzas, Cienfuegos and Sancti Spiritus where more than half of the country's 156 mills are to be found. However, traders who have inspected the damage report that the situation in the cane fields looks worse than it really is. Little, if any, of the cane is yet fully ripe so most of it will recover. Installations, however, have suffered serious damage, particularly in the province of Cienfuegos so the size of next season's crop will depend more upon how quickly the country's infrastructure can be repaired than on the availability of cane. The crop in 1995/96 amounted to 4.530 million tonnes, raw value. It was hoped that the 1996/97 crop would yield at least half a million tonnes more; this now looks doubtful.
Libya has bought two cargoes of 45 ICUMSA white sugar at $382.00 a tonne, c&f, for December delivery.
